# Docket 1.3.65

Four checks were wrong about a site rather than about a page. Three were found
by writing the pages that describe them; the fourth by running the shipped build
against our own site.

**A broken-link finding that downloaded the link.** Checking an outbound link to
a large file followed its redirect with a GET and began pulling the file — up to
eight megabytes — and reported the link as broken when that did not finish in
time. Any site whose download link points at an installer, a PDF or a video
could be told its download was dead when it was not. A redirect is now followed
with another HEAD; the GET confirmation stays where it was earned, on a real
failure.

**Author markup that could not satisfy the check that asked for it.**
`content.no_author` printed `"author": {"@type": "Person", ...}` as its own
remedy and then looked for a schema type called "author". There is no such type
— `author` is a property — so a site that did exactly what the report said saw
the same finding again. It also credited any page containing the word
"authored", so a privacy policy could silence the finding for a whole site. Both
halves now do what their names say.

**A question in your footer silenced the AI-extractability finding.** Question
headings were read from the whole document while the pages being judged were
counted from main content only, so one "Ready to get started?" in a footer
template made every page look answered. A heading that appears on every
substantial page is now treated as chrome.

**Sites that compress correctly were told to enable compression.** Docket asks
for gzip and deflate, so a server offering only Brotli answers uncompressed, as
the HTTP specification requires — and was reported at high severity with the
remedy "enable compression". The finding now says what was actually observed and
hands you the one command that tells the two cases apart before you change
anything.
